---
title: "Exercise 2.4"
---


## Solution

(I think it is *$A_j \in \mathcal{M}_j$* in exercise, not *$A_j\in \mathcal{M}$*)
<br>

Consider $A_n = \{2,4, \cdots, 2n\}$ and $\mathcal{M}_n = \{\emptyset, A_n, \mathbb{N}\}$. It is straightforward to verify that

(1) $\mathcal{M}_n$ is a monotone class, and

(2) $A_n \uparrow A = \{2,4,6, \cdots\}$.

However, $A \neq A_n \text{ for every } n$, so, $A \notin \mathcal{M}$.
